questions.question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Pedestrians waiting on the sidewalk for a walk signal.

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to all vehicles, pedestrians, and bicycles moving on their green light.

questions.question: When parallel parking facing downhill, how should you position your wheels?

options.text: Turn them sharply toward the curb or edge of the road.
Turn them away from the curb or edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them sharply toward the curb or edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb. This stops your car from rolling into traffic if your brakes fail.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle with lights or a siren, what should you do?

options.text: Stop right away and let the vehicle pass.
Drive to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
Slow down and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
questions.explanation: Move to the right side of the road and stop as soon as it is safe. Do not stop in an intersection. This lets the emergency vehicle pass quickly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you an intersection is ahead. Be ready to slow down, stop, or turn.

questions.question: Which statement is true about motorcycles?

options.text: Other drivers can follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with a single rider.
When passing a motorcycle, move completely into the left lane.
Motorcycle brake lights always turn on when the rider slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: When passing a motorcycle, move completely into the left lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use a full lane. Your entire vehicle must be in the left lane before and while passing a motorcycle.

questions.question: On an interstate, traffic is merging from on-ramps to your right. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane.

questions.explanation: When you see an on-ramp ahead, move left when traffic allows. This gives merging traffic more room to enter safely.

questions.question: An oncoming vehicle is heading toward you in your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.

questions.explanation: First, honk to get the other driver's attention. Steer right to escape. Brake hard and steady. Steering left could cause a head-on crash if the other driver swerves at the last second.

questions.question: A green arrow turns into a solid green light. What can you do?

options.text: You can still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You cannot turn anymore. You must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You do not have to turn in that direction anymore.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When the green arrow becomes a solid green light, you may still turn in that direction. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and vehicles coming toward you.

questions.question: Is it illegal for a car to share a lane with a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use a full lane. Cars must never try to share a lane with a motorcycle. Two motorcycles may share a lane with each other.

questions.question: What does a speed restriction sign show?

options.text: It can be ignored in rain, snow, or ice.
It is blue with black letters.
It shows a safe speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It shows a safe speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Speed advisory signs suggest a safe driving speed for curves and turns. You should follow these speeds in all weather. In rain, snow, or ice, you should drive even slower.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can turn left only after you stop.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign means left turns are prohibited.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. You should:

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Get ready to stop; the light will turn red soon.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means go slowly and look both ways before entering the intersection.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians crossing the street, whether in a marked crosswalk or not. Safety is the priority.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers surprise each other. Signal when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your horn when needed. Let other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know what you are doing.

questions.question: A slow-moving vehicle emblem looks like:
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this sign are going 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: On a vertical traffic light, red is on top and green is on bottom. On a horizontal light, red is on the left and green is on the right.

questions.question: You can pass on a two-lane road with a solid yellow line on your side.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line means no passing. You can only pass when there is a broken yellow line on your side of the road.

questions.question: A solid red HAWK signal means:

options.text: Drivers should slow down and get ready to stop.

questions.explanation: HAWK signals control pedestrian crossings. A solid red light means you must stop.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before turning left, look:
questions.explanation: Always look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, you should:

options.text: Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill, turn your wheels away from the curb. If your brakes fail, the car will roll toward the curb instead of into traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.
There is a bump in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn you about hazards ahead. This sign tells you to drive carefully when the road is wet because it may be slippery and harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: How far must you stay away from a fire hydrant when parking?
questions.explanation: You cannot park within eight feet of a fire hydrant. Park only where you will not block traffic and where other drivers can clearly see your vehicle.

questions.question: Why should you be careful when passing a bicycle?

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road.
questions.explanation: A cyclist may suddenly swerve into traffic to avoid obstacles on the road. Always drive carefully around bicycles.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and easier to miss than cars. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge how far away a motorcycle is or how fast it is going. Always be extra careful around motorcycles.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction on slippery roads. Slow down and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: What should you do if your car starts to skid?
questions.explanation: If your car skids, stay off the brakes. Keep steering until your car is under control and moving safely.

questions.question: How long does it take a fully loaded tractor-trailer to stop at 55 mph?
questions.explanation: Large trucks need much longer to stop than cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer needs almost 400 feet to stop when going 55 mph.

questions.question: Two cars reach a four-way stop at the same time. The other car is on your left. Who goes first?

options.text: The car on your left goes first.
Whoever is signaling a turn goes first.

questions.explanation: When two cars arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the car on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: How should you check traffic when entering a freeway?

options.text: Use your rearview and side mirrors.
Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic when entering a freeway. This helps you see vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Signal as you move into the next lane.
Signal 500 feet before on residential streets.

questions.explanation: Other cars and motorcycles can hide in your blind spot. Look over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet before changing lanes on residential streets. Signal five seconds before changing lanes on freeways.
